question_text: A 72-year-old patient presents to the emergency department because of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fever. He was started on levofloxacin for community-acquired pneumonia 2 weeks prior with resolution of his pulmonary symptoms. He has had hypertension for 20 years, for which he takes amlodipine. His temperature is 38.3°C (101.0°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. On examination, mild abdominal distension with minimal tenderness was found. Laboratory tests reveal a peripheral white blood cell count of 12.000/mm3 and a stool guaiac mildly positive for occult blood. Which of the following best describe the mechanism of this patient illness?

                    ### Question
                    A 72-year-old patient presents to the emergency department because of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fever. He was started on levofloxacin for community-acquired pneumonia 2 weeks prior with resolution of his pulmonary symptoms. He has had hypertension for 20 years, for which he takes amlodipine. His temperature is 38.3°C (101.0°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. On examination, mild abdominal distension with minimal tenderness was found. Laboratory tests reveal a peripheral white blood cell count of 12.000/mm3 and a stool guaiac mildly positive for occult blood. Which of the following best describe the mechanism of this patient illness?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Disruption of normal bowel flora and infection by spore-forming rods
opb. Autoimmune inflammation of the rectum
opc. Damage to the gastrointestinal tract by enteropathogenic viruses
opd. Decreased blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract
ope. Presence of osmotically active, poorly absorbed solutes in the bowel lumen

The presence of osmotically active, poorly absorbed solutes in the bowel lumen may also contribute to the abdominal pain and diarrhea. Autoimmune inflammation of the rectum and decreased blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract are less likely based on the presented information and standard medical knowledge.
